# Jubilees Chapter 4 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Cain and Abel; Seth; Enoch

---

**4:1** In the third week of the second jubilee, Eve gave birth to Cain. In the fourth week, Abel. In the fifth week, a daughter named Awan.

**4:2** In the first year of the third jubilee, Cain murdered Abel. The reason: God had accepted Abel's sacrifice and rejected Cain's.

**4:3** Cain struck him down in the open field. The blood of Abel cried out from the ground all the way to heaven, demanding justice for the killing.

**4:4** The LORD confronted Cain over what he had done to Abel, condemned him to wander the earth as a fugitive for his brother's blood, and cursed him.

**4:5** Because of this, the heavenly tablets record: "Cursed is the one who kills his neighbor without warning. Let everyone who witnessed it say, 'So be it.' And whoever saw it and stayed silent — let him be cursed just as the killer."

**4:6** That is why we reported to the LORD our God what Cain had done — the murder of Abel — so it could never be hushed up.

**4:7** Cain was sentenced to darkness, banished from God's presence, because he had killed his brother.

**4:8** He was cut off from the light forever. He settled in the land of Naid, the land where Adam had once lived.

**4:9** There he built a city and named it after his son Enoch.

**4:10** Adam was intimate with his wife again, and she conceived and bore a son. He named him Seth, explaining: "God has given us another child in Abel's place, since Cain killed him."

**4:11** In the sixth week, Adam and his wife had a daughter named Azura.

**4:12** Cain married his sister Awan, and she bore him Enoch near the end of the fourth jubilee. In the first year of the fifth jubilee's first week, the first permanent houses appeared on the earth — and Cain built a city.

**4:13** That Enoch married a woman named Mualet, daughter of Madai son of Jared — one of the daughters born after Abel's death.

**4:14** She bore Irad; Irad fathered Mehujael; Mehujael fathered Methushael; Methushael fathered Lamech.

**4:15** In the eleventh jubilee, in the fourth week, a man named Jared married Baraka, daughter of Rasujal. In the fifth week, in the fourth year of the jubilee, she gave birth to a son he named Enoch.

**4:16** This Enoch — the son of Jared — was the first human being born on earth to master writing, knowledge, and wisdom. He catalogued the movements of the stars by their monthly cycles in a written book, so that future generations could track the calendar by those patterns.

**4:17** He was history's first author of a formal testimony. He gave public witness to every generation on earth, explaining the jubilee weeks, teaching people the count of the years and months, and setting down the sabbatical year cycles — exactly as the angels had revealed them to him.

**4:18** In his dream-visions, Enoch saw the past and the future — everything that would happen to humanity from his own day until the final judgment. He saw it all, understood it all, wrote it all down. He left his testimony on earth as a permanent record for all humanity and every generation to come.

**4:19** In the twelfth jubilee, in the seventh week, Enoch married Edna, daughter of Danel. In the sixth year of that week, she bore him a son named Methuselah.

**4:20** For six full jubilee-periods, Enoch walked alongside the angels of God. They showed him everything — on earth and in the heavens, the workings of the sun and sky — and he wrote it all down.

**4:21** He gave testimony against the Watchers for their sin, and against the people who followed them. That testimony still stands as evidence against them in the record. He documented everything: what the Watchers did, what their sons and wives did, how they corrupted themselves, how they sinned, and what punishment and judgment fell on them.

**4:22** Then he was lifted up from among humanity, and the angels escorted him into the garden of Eden in great honor. There he continues to write — the record of the world's condemnation and judgment, and all the evil committed by human beings.

**4:23** Because of all this wickedness, God sent the floodwaters over the whole region of Eden. Enoch was placed there as a witness and a sign against all of humanity — to document the deeds of every generation until the final day of reckoning.

**4:24** There in the garden, Enoch burned the holy incense — sweet-smelling spices that rose before the LORD — on the mountain.

**4:25** For there are four places on earth that belong to the LORD: the garden of Eden, the Mountain of the East, Mount Sinai where you stand right now, and Mount Zion — which in the age of new creation will be consecrated as the holy center of the earth. Through these four holy sites, the earth will be cleansed of all its guilt and impurity for every generation.

**4:26** In the fourteenth jubilee, in the third week, Methuselah married Edna, daughter of Azrial. She bore him a son in the fifth week, whom Methuselah named Lamech.

**4:27** In the fifteenth jubilee, third week, third year, Lamech married a woman named Betenos. She bore him a son he named Noah, saying: "This one will bring us relief from all the hard work and exhaustion this cursed earth has cost us."

**4:28** In the nineteenth jubilee, seventh week, sixth year, Adam died. His sons buried him in his homeland — the land of his creation. He was the first person ever to be buried in the ground.

**4:29** He fell seventy years short of a thousand. And a thousand years is equivalent to one day in the reckoning of heaven. So when God said about the tree of knowledge, "On the day you eat from it you will die" — Adam died within that very day. He never completed it.

**4:30** That same jubilee year, just after Adam died, Cain was killed. His own house collapsed on him and crushed him with its stones — because he had once killed his brother with a stone, and now a stone killed him. Justice was exact.

**4:31** That is why the heavenly tablets decree: whatever weapon a man uses to kill someone, the same weapon will be used to kill him. Whatever he did to his victim, the same will be done to him.

**4:32** In the twenty-fifth jubilee, fifth week, first year, Noah married a woman named Emzara. In the third year she gave birth to Shem; in the fifth year, Ham; and in the first year of the sixth week, Japheth.

---
*PNEUMA notes: Enoch's description (vv.16-25) is rendered to highlight his role as civilizational founder (writing), calendar-keeper, prophetic witness, and temple priest. "Dream-visions" (v.18) follows the Ge'ez term. "Final judgment" for "day of condemnation" makes eschatological sense clear.*
